meta.title: Timeless: The Valley of Dry Bones
meta.verseText: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the human heart.
meta.theme: God is with us at all times, breathing new life and hope into every situation.

questions.text: What is the Big Idea for this week's lesson?
options: God is with us at all times.
questions.hint: It's about God always being near.
questions.explanation: The Big Idea for this lesson is 'God is with us at all times,' which powers the whole message about God's constant presence.

questions.text: Who was the prophet God showed the valley of dry bones?
questions.hint: His name starts with 'E.'
questions.explanation: Ezekiel was the prophet God spoke through, and God showed him the vision of the valley of dry bones in Ezekiel 37.

questions.text: What did God ask Ezekiel about the dry bones?
questions.hint: It's a question about life.
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 37:3, God asked Ezekiel, 'Can these bones live?' — a question that seemed impossible but showed God's power.

questions.text: The bones in Ezekiel's vision were 'dry,' which means the bodies had died a long time ago.
questions.hint: Dry bones = very old bones.
questions.explanation: True. The lesson explains the bones were dry because they belonged to bodies that had died and decayed a long time ago.

questions.text: What happened after Ezekiel spoke to the bones as God told him?
options: They connected and were covered with skin
questions.hint: The bones came together.
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 37:7-8, the bones came together, connected to each other, and were covered with skin.

questions.text: What finally made the bodies stand up and move?
options: A strong wind blew them up
questions.hint: Think about God's breath and Spirit.
questions.explanation: God breathed life into the bodies, and they stood up and moved — becoming a great army of living, breathing people.

questions.text: The valley of dry bones turned into a large army of living, breathing people.
questions.hint: Remember what happened at the end of the vision.
questions.explanation: True. In Ezekiel 37:10, the bones became a vast army of living people once God's breath filled them.

questions.text: Where had God's people been taken away to during Ezekiel's time?
questions.hint: A powerful empire captured them.
questions.explanation: God's people had been taken away to Babylon, and their temple and city had been destroyed, which is why they felt hopeless.

questions.text: During what time period did the vision of dry bones take place?
questions.hint: It was long before Jesus was born.
questions.explanation: The lesson places Ezekiel in the 6th century BCE, when God's people were in exile in Babylon.

questions.text: The dry bones coming to life reminds us of when God ______ life into the first humans in Genesis.
questions.hint: Same word used for how the bones came alive.
questions.explanation: God breathed life into the first humans in Genesis, just as God breathed life into the dry bones in Ezekiel's vision.

questions.text: What did the dry bones represent about God's relationship with the people?
options: That the relationship had died out but God would restore it
questions.hint: Think about what was broken and what God would fix.
questions.explanation: The dry bones pictured how the people's relationship with God had 'died out' when they disobeyed, but God promised to put it back together again.

questions.text: What made the bones come to life in Ezekiel's vision?
questions.hint: It's God's way of being with us all the time.
questions.explanation: It was God's Spirit that made the bones come to life — God's way of being with us and living in us all the time.

questions.text: Why was it hard for the people in Babylon to believe God was still with them?
options: They were suffering far from home under a foreign empire
They had never heard of God
questions.hint: They had lost their homes and their temple.
questions.explanation: The people were removed from their homes and suffering under an empire that invaded their land, so it was hard to believe God was still near.

questions.text: The message of the dry bones was meant to give God's people ______.
questions.hint: The opposite of feeling hopeless.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel was God's messenger of hope; the vision promised the people that God was with them and would bring them home.

questions.text: According to the object lesson, a dry sponge is like a person without ______.
questions.hint: The sponge needs to be 'hydrated' to be useful.
questions.explanation: The dry sponge represents us without God's Spirit; when we 'soak up' the Spirit, God can do amazing things through us.

questions.text: According to the lesson, how can we 'soak up' the Holy Spirit?
options: By spending time in prayer, worship, and studying the Bible
questions.hint: Think prayer, worship, and Bible.
questions.explanation: The lesson says we soak up the Spirit by spending time in prayer, worship, and studying the Bible.

questions.text: The Hebrews passage was written after Jesus had lived, died, and came back to life.
questions.hint: Hebrews comes after the Gospels.
questions.explanation: True. Hebrews 13 was written after Jesus lived, died, and rose again, reminding us God is with us all the time.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: 'Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and ______.'
questions.hint: It means for all time.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:8 says, 'Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever,' showing God never changes.

questions.text: What is our very best helper, according to the Hebrews teaching?
questions.hint: Jesus sent this helper when he went to heaven.
questions.explanation: The best helper we have is the Holy Spirit, whom Jesus sent to be with us when he went up to heaven.

questions.text: Besides the Holy Spirit, what other helpers does God give us?
options: Leaders, parents, and trustworthy people who teach us about God
questions.hint: Think of the caring people around you.
questions.explanation: God gives us helpers like leaders, parents, and other trustworthy people who love us and teach us about God.

questions.text: In Ezekiel 37:1, Ezekiel said that '______ of the Lord' was with him.
questions.hint: It's a body part that protects and guides.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:1 says 'the hand of the Lord' was with him, meaning God was near to protect, comfort, and guide him.

questions.text: Being in 'God's hands' is meant to make us feel afraid and alone.
questions.hint: God's hands protect and comfort us.
questions.explanation: False. Being in God's hands should make us feel safe, because it means God is near to protect, comfort, and guide us.

questions.text: What is this month's overall theme called?
questions.hint: It's about time and God being with us through all of it.
questions.explanation: The month's theme is 'Timeless,' and this is the final week of the series.

questions.text: What does the memory verse say God has set in the human heart?
questions.hint: It means forever, no beginning or end.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 3:11a says God 'has also set eternity in the human heart,' showing we are made to know the God who is timeless.

questions.text: When we go through hard times, what can we remember from this lesson?
options: God is with us in every situation
Hard times mean God is angry
questions.hint: It's the Big Idea.
questions.explanation: The lesson teaches that even in the hardest times, God is with us in every single situation we face.

questions.text: What is one way you can remember God's presence when you're worried or stressed?
options: Take a deep breath, pray, or read your Bible
questions.hint: The response activity gave some ideas.
questions.explanation: The lesson suggests taking a deep breath, praying, or reading your Bible to remember God is with you.

questions.text: How can we learn about God from the helpers he gives us?
options: By watching how they follow God and hearing their stories
questions.hint: It's more than just what they say.
questions.explanation: We learn not just from helpers' words but by watching how they follow God and hearing their stories of how God is with them.

questions.text: What did the 'Always There Art' bookmark activity teach about God's presence?
options: God's presence can be hard to see but is always there
God is only there on Sundays
questions.hint: Hidden words revealed by paint.
questions.explanation: Like white crayon words revealed by watercolor, God's presence can be hard to see or feel sometimes, but God is always there and close by.

questions.text: God promised the exiled people that he would bring them ______.
questions.hint: They wanted to return from Babylon.
questions.explanation: God promised through Ezekiel that the people would have hope of returning home and to a loving relationship with God.

questions.text: Because we live in the future from Ezekiel's time, we know God kept his promise to bring the people home.
questions.hint: History shows what happened next.
questions.explanation: True. The lesson points out that we, living after Ezekiel, can see that God kept his promise to bring the people back home.

questions.text: What did Ezekiel do to the bones to make them start coming together?
options: He spoke God's message to them
questions.hint: God told him to prophesy, or speak, to them.
questions.explanation: God told Ezekiel to speak (prophesy) to the bones, and when he did, they began connecting together.

questions.text: According to Hebrews, why don't we have to be afraid of what happens?
questions.hint: God stands beside us.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:6 reminds us we can be confident because God is our helper, so we don't have to be afraid.

questions.text: The dry bones could bring themselves back to life without any help from God.
questions.hint: It took a miracle from God.
questions.explanation: False. Only God could bring the dry bones to life; it was a miracle done by God's power and Spirit.

story.summary: During a hard time when God's people had been taken far from home to Babylon, God gave the prophet Ezekiel an amazing vision. God set Ezekiel down in a valley full of dry bones and asked, 'Can these bones live?' When Ezekiel spoke God's message, the bones rattled together, grew skin, and God breathed life into them until they became a huge army of living people. The vision was God's promise that even though the people felt hopeless and far from home, God was still with them and would bring them back. The New Testament reminds us that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that the Holy Spirit is our best helper. No matter what we face, God is with us at all times.

scenes.title: A Sad Time Far From Home
scenes.description: God's people had turned away from him and were carried off to Babylon, where their temple and city were destroyed. They felt hopeless, as if God had left them. But God was already planning to give them hope through a prophet named Ezekiel.

scenes.title: The Valley of Dry Bones
scenes.description: God set Ezekiel down in a valley full of dry bones and asked, 'Can these bones live?' The bones were dry because they had been dead a long time. It seemed impossible, but God was about to show his incredible power.

scenes.title: Bones Come to Life
scenes.description: God told Ezekiel to speak to the bones. As he did, the bones rattled together, joined, and were covered with skin. Then God breathed his Spirit into them, and they stood up as a great army of living, breathing people.

scenes.title: God's Promise of Hope
scenes.description: The dry bones showed how the people's relationship with God had dried up, but God promised to restore it and bring them home. The vision gave the people hope that God had not abandoned them.

scenes.title: God Is With Us Forever
scenes.description: Hebrews reminds us that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that God gives us helpers—especially the Holy Spirit. We can remember God's presence by praying, worshiping, and reading the Bible, trusting that God is with us at all times.
